user.title: Connect to Wiser for KNX
user.description: Enter the connection details for your Wiser for KNX (or spaceLYnk / LogicMachine) controller.

data.plain_http: Use plain HTTP instead of HTTPS (insecure — the controller password is sent unencrypted)

data_description.plain_http: Leave off. With this on, the controller username and password, and the backup password, are sent unencrypted and can be read by anyone on your network. Only turn it on if the controller cannot serve HTTPS.
data_description.skip_verify: Leave off. Self-signed controllers are handled by confirming the certificate fingerprint in the next step. Turning this on sends your credentials without checking who answers.

credentials.title: Wiser for KNX Authentication
credentials.description: Wiser for KNX was discovered at {host}. Please provide credentials to access the local API.

data.plain_http: Use plain HTTP instead of HTTPS (insecure — the controller password is sent unencrypted)

data_description.plain_http: Leave off. With this on, the controller username and password, and the backup password, are sent unencrypted and can be read by anyone on your network. Only turn it on if the controller cannot serve HTTPS.
data_description.skip_verify: Leave off. Self-signed controllers are handled by confirming the certificate fingerprint in the next step. Turning this on sends your credentials without checking who answers.

reauth_confirm.title: Reauthenticate Wiser for KNX
reauth_confirm.description: The controller at {host} rejected the stored credentials. Enter the current username and password.

backup.title: Controller backups
backup.description: Back up this controller from Home Assistant. Leave the password empty to skip backups for now; you can set them up later under Configure. The password protects the backup files and must have at least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a digit.

trust_certificate.title: Trust this controller's certificate?
trust_certificate.description:
The controller at {host} uses a certificate that Home Assistant cannot verify (normal for a self-signed controller).

SHA-256 fingerprint:
`{fingerprint}`

Compare it with the fingerprint shown by the controller. Submitting trusts only this exact certificate for this controller: Home Assistant will refuse any other certificate and ask you again. If you cannot confirm the fingerprint, someone on your network may be impersonating the controller and could capture your password; cancel in that case.

reauth_certificate.title: Controller certificate changed
reauth_certificate.description:
The certificate presented by {host} is not trusted.

New SHA-256 fingerprint:
`{fingerprint}`
Previously trusted: {previous}

A rotated or reinstalled controller certificate is a normal cause. A different device or an attacker on your network would look the same. Only submit if you have confirmed this fingerprint on the controller.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to Wiser for KNX on the specified host/port (the address answered, but not like the controller API).
error.invalid_auth: Authentication failed. Please verify username and password.
error.invalid_backup_password: The backup password must have at least 8 characters, with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a digit.
error.untrusted_certificate: The controller's certificate is not trusted.

abort.already_configured: Device is already configured in Home Assistant.
abort.not_wiser_knx: The device did not answer like a Wiser for KNX / KNX IoT controller. Check the address, or add it manually.
abort.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the controller.
abort.fingerprint_mismatch: The controller presented a different certificate than the one that was confirmed.

init.title: Wiser for KNX Options
init.description: Configure polling and controller backups. Backup password set: {backup_set}. Leave the password empty to keep the current one. The controller requires at least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a digit.

data.plain_http: Use plain HTTP instead of HTTPS (insecure — the controller password is sent unencrypted)

data_description.port: The controller port, 1 to 65535. Switching plain HTTP on or off changes a port left at 443 or 80 to the matching default (80 or 443); any other port is kept as entered.
data_description.plain_http: Leave off. With this on, the controller username and password, and the backup password, are sent unencrypted and can be read by anyone on your network. Only turn it on if the controller cannot serve HTTPS.
data_description.skip_verify: Off is recommended. Turning it on removes any trusted certificate fingerprint. Turning it off again re-checks the certificate and asks you to confirm its fingerprint if it is self-signed.

error.invalid_backup_password: The backup password must have at least 8 characters, with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a digit.
error.invalid_port: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.

create_backup.name: Create controller backup
create_backup.description: Download the system and project backups from the controller and store them in the wiser_backups folder of the Home Assistant configuration directory.

insecure_tls.title: Certificate verification is disabled
insecure_tls.description: The connection to the controller at {host} does not verify its TLS certificate, so the controller password is sent to whoever answers on that address. Open the integration, choose Configure, turn off "Skip certificate verification (insecure)", and confirm the controller's certificate fingerprint when asked.

insecure_http.title: Connection to the controller is not encrypted
insecure_http.description: The connection to the controller at {host} uses plain HTTP, so the controller username and password are sent unencrypted on every update, and the backup password is sent unencrypted when a backup is made. Open the integration, choose Configure, and turn off "Use plain HTTP instead of HTTPS (insecure — the controller password is sent unencrypted)". If the controller cannot serve HTTPS, this notice stays.
